admission.justification: Realized across markdown_mask.py, validate/jargon.py and site/markdown_transforms.py and proved by five golden tests in tests/unit/test_markdown_mask.py; prevents duplicate scanner drift, line-offset bugs on CRLF inputs, and inverted validate-to-site package imports.

applicability: Shared low-level Markdown fenced-code, inline-code, math-end and directive-close primitives in src/rh_pipeline/markdown_mask.py consumed by validate/jargon.py and site/markdown_transforms.py.
conditions: src/rh_pipeline/markdown_mask.py imports only stdlib re (zero ConceptCard or SiteBuildError dependencies) and sits below both validate and site in the import graph.

mask_fenced_code, mask_inline_code and mask_code_spans preserve exact character lengths and LF/CRLF line endings across nested/odd backticks and paragraph breaks; site/markdown_transforms.py re-exports mask_code_spans and mask_fenced_code.
exclusions: Prose-specific link/math scanning remains in validate/jargon.py and site-specific directive expansion remains in site/markdown_transforms.py.

evidence: tests/unit/test_markdown_mask.py (CRLF, nested/odd backticks, math-in-code, directives-in-math, braces, neutrality, re-exports) in scripts/check-quality.sh

statement: Low-level Markdown code, math, and directive masking primitives live in neutral rh_pipeline.markdown_mask below both validate and site, preserving exact same-length offsets across LF and CRLF inputs and re-exporting mask_code_spans from site.markdown_transforms.
title: Neutral same-length Markdown masking primitives below validate and site
